name: PNC-27
lead: PNC-27 is a 32-residue chimeric peptide that joins a segment of the p53 tumour-suppressor protein (residues 12-26, the region that binds HDM-2/MDM2) to a membrane-penetrating sequence [1][2]. In laboratory studies its authors report that it kills cancer cells, but not normal cells, by binding HDM-2 on the cancer-cell membrane and forming pores that lyse the cell [2][8].

All published evidence is from cell lines and laboratory models; no human clinical trial has been published. It is sold by research-peptide vendors and is not an approved medicine. The sources reviewed contain no documented looksmaxxing-community discussion; it is listed under longevity-oriented peptides.

paras: NMR studies determined the solution structure of PNC-27 and described its selective, rapid membrane-disrupting (necrotic) action on a range of human cancer cell lines [1]. A 2010 PNAS study reported that the p53 portion adopts an HDM-2-binding conformation and that the peptide kills cancer cells by binding HDM-2 in their membranes [2]. A 2022 paper describes the binding as inducing membrane-pore formation [8].

Studies of the related PNC-28 reported necrosis rather than apoptosis in pancreatic cancer cells, attributed to the penetratin sequence [7]. Work on leukemia cell lines reported dependence on membrane HDM-2 expression [6], and a separate 2020 study found membrane HDM2 on acute myeloid leukemia blasts but not on normal haematopoietic stem cells [4]. The intact peptide, rather than fragments, was reported to lyse tumour cells [5].

No studies found in humans. Laboratory research includes cell-line cytotoxicity work, a report of synergy with paclitaxel in ovarian cancer models [10], use of PNC-27 and PNC-28 as targeting moieties for gene-delivery carriers [3], and computational docking analyses [9].
PNC-27 is marketed by research-peptide suppliers for laboratory use. The sources reviewed describe no regulatory approval and no documented community protocols.

timeline.event: NMR solution structure of PNC-27 reported [1].
PNC-28 reported to cause necrosis of pancreatic cancer cells [7].
PNC-27 reported to bind HDM-2 in cancer-cell membranes [2].
Review of PNC-27 pore formation and HDM-2 binding published [8].

card.summary: A p53-derived peptide shown to lyse cancer cells in lab studies; no human trials, sold only as a research chemical.
card.note: Cell-line data only; no human safety or efficacy data.

quick.overview:
PNC-27 fuses a piece of the p53 tumour-suppressor protein to a cell-penetrating sequence. In lab experiments it is reported to rupture cancer cells while sparing normal ones.

The evidence is entirely preclinical. No human trial results are published, and no appearance use is documented in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: It is reported to bind HDM-2 protein displayed on cancer-cell membranes and to form pores that cause the cell to burst.
quick.risks: Human safety is unstudied. It is not an approved drug; it is sold as a research chemical.
